newsitem.title: USA: Carp to vacuum clogged Miami canals.
newsitem.headline: Carp to vacuum clogged Miami canals.

text.p: Here's a tale about some fish that Miami authorities hope will not get away.
More than 5,000 carp will be released into Dade County canals next month with the task of gobbling up weeds that are clogging the system. Tractors and chemicals now do the job.
"We're trying this new method to save money and keep the canals clean," South Florida Water Management spokeswoman Maribel Balbin told Reuters.
The canals are used for flood control and boating. The weeds, especially fast-growing hydrilla, hamper the ability to control water flows, but they are the carps' favourite food.

The fish cost about $3.50 each and will be collected from farms in Florida and elsewhere in the southeast. Authorities expect to lose some to predators but hope that as most grow more than a foot (30 cm) long they will be able to fend for themselves.
"They do grow kind of big so they should be around for a while," Balbin said. "We'll put up signs asking fishermen to dump them back if they catch one."
